proposals.before: In his youth he served on the staff of the Prince of Qin; he followed him on campaigns and distinguished himself, rising through the posts of Left Armor Guard and Cavalry General and receiving the title heir of Quanjiao County.
proposals.after: In his youth he served on the staff of the Prince of Qin; he followed him on campaigns and distinguished himself, rising through the posts of Left Armor Guard and Cavalry General and receiving the title viscount of Quanjiao County.
proposals.reason: 縣子 is a viscount-rank noble title, not an heir apparent; 'heir' mistranslates 子 in 全椒縣子.

proposals.before: In youth he served in the Prince of Qin's staff; following campaigns and punitive expeditions he had merit, was promoted through Left Armor Guard and Cavalry General, and enfeoffed as heir of Quanjiao County.
proposals.after: In youth he served in the Prince of Qin's staff; following campaigns and punitive expeditions he had merit, was promoted through Left Armor Guard and Cavalry General, and enfeoffed as viscount of Quanjiao County.
proposals.reason: Same error as the idiomatic line: 全椒縣子 is viscount of Quanjiao County, not heir.

proposals.before: He also sent Chushi to tell Chengan: "The Prince of Wei enjoys favor; if Your Majesty should issue a summons, I beg you not to enter lightly."
proposals.after: He also sent Chushi to tell Chengan: "The Prince of Wei enjoys favor; if the emperor should issue a summons, I beg you not to enter lightly."
proposals.reason: 陛下 in the warning is the reigning emperor, not Chengqian; the literal 'Your Majesty' makes the crown prince the referent of 陛下.

proposals.before: __FORCETOC__Zhang Liang was a native of Xingyang in Zheng Prefecture.
proposals.after: Zhang Liang was a native of Xingyang in Zheng Prefecture.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English is prefixed with a wiki/table-of-contents marker __FORCETOC__ that is not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: __FORCETOC__Zhang Liang — Zhang Liang, a native of Xingyang in Zheng Prefecture.
proposals.after: Zhang Liang was a native of Xingyang in Zheng Prefecture.
proposals.reason: The literal English inserts a TOC token and duplicates the name; neither is in the Chinese sentence.

proposals.before: He was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then sent out as military governor of Luo.
proposals.after: He was appointed Chief Steward of the Household of the Heir Apparent, then sent out as military governor of Luo.
proposals.reason: 太子詹事 is the household steward of the heir, not Grand Mentor (太傅).

proposals.before: He was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then sent out as military governor of Luo Prefecture.
proposals.after: He was appointed Chief Steward of the Household of the Heir Apparent, then sent out as military governor of Luo Prefecture.
proposals.reason: Same office mistranslation of 太子詹事 as Grand Mentor.

proposals.before: A diviner named Cheng Gongying, whom Liang had long favored, heard him say in private, "You once declared that His Majesty was the true ruler of all under Heaven — how prescient you were!"
proposals.after: A diviner named Cheng Gongying, whom Liang had long favored, was told by him in private, "You once declared that His Majesty was the true ruler of all under Heaven — how prescient you were!"
proposals.reason: 陰謂曰 takes Liang as speaker addressing Cheng; the idiomatic English reverses the speech direction.

proposals.before: __FORCETOC__Xue Wanjun was originally from Dunhuang and later moved to Xianyang in the capital district.
proposals.after: Xue Wanjun was originally from Dunhuang and later moved to Xianyang in the capital district.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English is prefixed with a TOC marker not present in the historical prose.

proposals.before: __FORCETOC__Xue Wanjun — Xue Wanjun, originally a man of Dunhuang, later moved to Xianyang in Jingzhao.
proposals.after: Xue Wanjun, originally a man of Dunhuang, later moved to Xianyang in Jingzhao.
proposals.reason: Removes the TOC token and the duplicated English name introduced before the biographical clause.

proposals.before: When Yi submitted to Tang, Gaozu made Wanjun Supreme Pillar of State and Duke of Yong'an.
proposals.after: When he and Yi submitted, Gaozu made Wanjun Supreme Pillar of State and Duke of Yong'an.
proposals.reason: 與藝歸款 means Wanjun submitted together with Luo Yi; the idiomatic English makes only Yi the subject.

proposals.before: He was appointed commander of the Left Unicorn Guard.
proposals.after: He was appointed general of the Left Garrison Guard.
proposals.reason: 左屯衛將軍 is the Left Tunwei (Garrison) Guard, not a Unicorn Guard.

proposals.before: He was appointed Left Commander of the Unicorn Guard.
proposals.after: He was appointed Left General of the Garrison Guard.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 屯衛 as Unicorn Guard.

proposals.before: Later, when the emperor visited Furong Garden, he was imprisoned for impropriety in the Pure Palace and died of grief and resentment.
proposals.after: Later, when the emperor visited Furong Garden, Wanjun was imprisoned for negligence in clearing the palace and died of grief and resentment.
proposals.reason: 坐 here means being charged with an offense, not sitting; 清宮不謹 is failure to clear the palace properly for the visit, not sexual impropriety in a hall named Pure Palace.

proposals.before: Later when the Emperor visited Furong Garden, he sat in the Pure Palace with impropriety and was cast into prison; distressed and resentful, he died.
proposals.after: Later when the Emperor visited Furong Garden, he was charged with negligence in clearing the palace and cast into prison; distressed and resentful, he died.
proposals.reason: Literal 坐 is calqued as sat; 清宮 is the ritual clearing of the palace, not a place in which he sat improperly.

proposals.before: The enemy was terrified and withdrew to Bozhou.
proposals.after: The enemy was terrified and then closed in on Bozhuo city.
proposals.reason: 傅泊汋城 means they pressed upon the city 泊汋; 泊汋 is the toponym, not a withdrawal to Bozhou.

proposals.before: The barbarians were all shaken with terror and thereupon moored at Bozhou city.
proposals.after: The barbarians were all shaken with terror and thereupon pressed upon Bozhuo city.
proposals.reason: 泊汋 is a place-name; 傅 is to press against, not to moor a boat.

proposals.before: Appended: Lu Zushang — Lu Zushang, courtesy name Jiliang, was from Le'an in Guangzhou.
proposals.after: Appended: Lu Zushang — Lu Zushang, courtesy name Jiliang, was from Le'an in Guang Prefecture.
proposals.reason: Chinese 光州 is Guang Prefecture, not the city Guangzhou (廣州); the literal already has Guang Prefecture.

proposals.before: On the Prince of Zhao's campaign against Fu Gongshi he served as vanguard, took Xuan and She, advanced against Feng Huiliang and Chen Zhengtong, and defeated them.
proposals.after: Following Li Xiaogong, Prince of Zhao Commandery, against Fu Gongshi, he served as vanguard commander, took Xuan and She, advanced against the rebel leaders Feng Huiliang and Chen Zhengtong, and defeated them.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic drops 孝恭 and 前軍總管; 趙郡王 is Prince of Zhao Commandery, not merely Prince of Zhao.

proposals.before: Soon he led the Shandong route army with Prince Yong'an Xiaoji against Lü Chongmao at Xia; the army was beaten and he was taken.
proposals.after: Soon he led the east-of-Shan (陝東) route army with Prince Yong'an Xiaoji against Lü Chongmao at Xia; the army was beaten and he was taken.
proposals.reason: 陝東道 is the circuit east of Mount Shan, not Shandong (山東).

proposals.before: Soon he also led the Shandong Route campaign command and followed Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji against Lü Chongmao at Xia county; the army was defeated and he was imprisoned by the rebels.
proposals.after: Soon he also led the east-of-Shan Route campaign command and followed Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji against Lü Chongmao at Xia county; the army was defeated and he was imprisoned by the rebels.
proposals.reason: Same error as the idiomatic: 陝東 is not Shandong.

proposals.before: When Shidu fell he was made prefect of Feng, then summoned as Right Commander of the Unicorn Guard.
proposals.after: When Shidu fell he was made prefect of Feng, then summoned as General of the Right Leading Army Guard.
proposals.reason: 右領軍衛將軍 is the Right Leading Army Guard, not an Unicorn Guard.

proposals.before: Earlier Xu Xuan of Changshe interpreted prophecy and told Lan, "Men say there is one who will live long as ruler — all say General Liu is destined for the throne."
proposals.after: Earlier Xu Xuan of Changshe interpreted the prophecy texts and told Lan, "The long-lived throughout the realm all say General Liu will become the ruler of the world."
proposals.reason: 長年者 are elders or the long-lived, not a future long-lived ruler; 咸言 is what they all say about General Liu, so the idiomatic version fuses two clauses and invents a separate destined sovereign.
